verdict_detail: All35questions and effective asked-scope keys are supported by the supplied base authority. Requested corrections distinguish givens/background without losing asked costs, actors, timing, conditions, exceptions or outcomes. Q35 closes the independently identified Banker assignment gap. No further source-supported previously unasked rule/outcome branch or consequential timing/priority/exception interaction survived challenge.
scope: Mayfair2010/2013 English2-4-player base with applicable previous-Mayfair unified clarifications only. Excludes Up!, Underworld, Americana, Con Jobs, revised2024six-player edition and optional Gamble Variant.

consistency_checks.historical_baseline_preservation: Manifest declaration recorded; baseline answer-key and v3 files were not opened. This review validates effective grading-key-v4 as an explicitly versioned asked-scope interpretation, not a silent historical rewrite.

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: How are starting properties and money assigned, where do the dealt cards go, and how is the End of Game card inserted?
asked_facts_reviewed: Remove End of Game, shuffle, deal two property cards per player.
Mark the two initial lots and take starting money equal to the sum of their printed card money values.
Discard by color/Strip with counts visible.
Divide remaining shuffled deck into four roughly equal stacks; End of Game on top of fourth, other three on top.
contextual_background_reviewed: These card values are only used during setup; Q03 asks that limitation explicitly.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Starting property/money assignment, card discards and End-card insertion remain required; setup-only limit correctly becomes context because Q03 asks it.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p2 Setting Up; unified p5

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: Who takes the first turn, how does turn order proceed, and what is the normal Draw/Play sequence?
asked_facts_reviewed: Each rolls two dice; highest roller takes player card and first turn.
Pass player card left after each turn.
Draw property card, take its lot, pay all owned lots, pay/score indicated casinos, discard appropriately, then Play actions.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Two-dice highest roller/player card, leftward order and complete normal Draw through discard then Play are asked and correct.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p2 Taking Turns/On Every Turn; p3 Ending Step 1

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: You draw the card for an empty lot. When is it acquired and paid, and do the printed card starting-money values pay again?
asked_facts_reviewed: Place your marker before payouts.
The newly acquired marked lot pays you $1 in the coming lot payout.
Card money values are used only during setup, not drawn-turn income.
contextual_background_reviewed: All other marked lots also pay their owners $1, tested by Q02/Q06.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: New marker precedes $1 lot payout; printed card starting-money values do not pay again. Other lots correctly contextual.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p2 Setting Up/Take Over Your Lot/Owned Lots Pay

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: You draw a lot card for a sprawled tile with an opponent’s 5, although the board prints 2. What happens to the tile and die, and who receives its imminent matching-color money?
asked_facts_reviewed: Tile stays; replace opposing die with your own retaining current value 5, not printed 2.
Acquisition precedes payouts, so you receive $5 for that die when its casino pays.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Replace opposing die at current5, retain tile, receive imminent $5. Printed2 is correctly rejected.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p2 Take Over Your Lot/Money Paid

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: When do same-color tiles form one casino, can they be divided, and is the boss determined by total pips or something else?
asked_facts_reviewed: Edge-connected same-color tiles on same block form a single indivisible casino; diagonal-only contact does not.
Boss is owner of highest individual die, not greatest total pips or most tiles.
contextual_background_reviewed: Casino colors do not denote player colors.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Same-block edge-connected same-color tiles form one indivisible casino; highest single die, not total. Color independence correctly contextual.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p1 Casino Tiles/Player Dice; p2 Who Owns What

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: A three-tile gold casino contains Red 5 and Blue 3 and 2; Red also owns two marked lots. On a gold payout, how much money and how many points does each receive from these holdings?
asked_facts_reviewed: Red receives $7: $5 die plus $2 lots.
Blue receives $5 from dice.
Red boss receives 3 casino points, Blue no casino points.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Red receives $7 and3 casino points; Blue receives $5 and0 casino points. Actors and payout sources correct.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p2 Owned Lots Pay/Money Paid/Points Earned

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: How does Pay The Strip differ from a color payout, and what qualifies a casino whose only one tile touches The Strip?
asked_facts_reviewed: Color pays all casinos of that color anywhere.
Strip pays all colors with at least one casino edge adjacent to Strip.
Entire qualifying casino pays money/points for all tiles, not only touching tile.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Matching color pays everywhere; Strip requires an edge and pays the whole qualifying casino across all colors.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p2 Pay Based on Color/Pay The Strip; unified p8

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: Which actions may you take in Play, in what order and how often, and may another player perform an action on your turn?
asked_facts_reviewed: Build, sprawl, remodel, reorganize, gamble in any order.
All may repeat except gamble once per own turn; reorganization also limited per die per turn.
No player takes actions on another player’s turn.
contextual_background_reviewed: Trading may occur at any time subject to exceptions; tested by Q17/Q27/Q32.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Exactly five base actions, any order; repeat except once-per-turn gamble and per-die reorganization limit; no off-turn action.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p3 Step 2 Play/Reorganize; p4 Trading

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: How do you build on your marked lot whose board price is $6 and printed die is 2? State cost, marker and die handling, and tile choice.
asked_facts_reviewed: Pay $6; choose available casino tile color.
Remove/reclaim marker, place tile on your owned lot and your die set to board value 2.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: $6, available color choice, reclaimed marker and own board-value2 die. Neighbor merger remains contextual.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p3 Build; unified p10 Build

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: You boss a gold casino and want to sprawl onto an edge-adjacent empty unowned $9 lot with printed die 3. What do you pay and place, and may you instead sprawl onto an opponent’s marked lot or a merely diagonal lot?
asked_facts_reviewed: Pay $18, place available gold tile with own die 3.
The stated eligible lot is empty/unowned and edge-adjacent; opponent-marked and diagonal-only targets are illegal.
Cannot sprawl without available tile of same color.
contextual_background_reviewed: The question already gives that the acting player is the casino boss; no need to restate a given as an extra fact.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: $18, available gold tile and own3, unowned empty edge target, reject opponent marker and diagonal. Given boss status now correctly background.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p3 Sprawl

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: How does remodeling a two-tile casino work, including eligibility, cost, tile supply, and a merger with a neighboring casino whose highest die beats yours?
asked_facts_reviewed: Must boss casino; remodel all its tiles into one new color with enough available tiles.
Pay $10 ($5 each); replace all tiles with new-color tiles; dice/holdings remain.
Edge-adjacent same-color casinos merge; owner of larger die becomes boss even if another player.
Return replaced old-color tiles to their supply.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Boss eligibility, all tiles, enough new color, $10, old tiles returned, dice remain and higher opposing die controls merger.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p3 Remodel and example; unified p11

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: May a non-boss with one die reorganize a casino with dice 5, 3 and 2? State who pays how much, which dice roll and who rolls them, and where multiple dice may return.
asked_facts_reviewed: Yes, at least one own die suffices; acting player pays $10 total pips of all dice.
All dice reroll, each owner rolling their own.
Each owner returns dice only to their own original tiles, choosing assignment among those tiles if multiple.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: One own die permits non-boss reorganization; actor pays $10 all-pip cost, all owners reroll their dice and can assign within own original tiles.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p3 Reorganize

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: A die was reorganized earlier this turn and its casino then merges into a larger casino. Can the larger casino be reorganized this turn, and are free boss-tie rerolls prohibited too?
asked_facts_reviewed: No: no die may be reorganized more than once per turn, so any previously reorganized die prevents reorganization of the enlarged casino.
Boss-tie rerolls are free and not subject to reorganization once-per-turn limit.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Previously reorganized die bars another reorganization after merge; free boss ties remain possible and mandatory.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p3 Reorganize; p4 Reroll if Tied; unified p11

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: After a merger, Red 5 and Blue 5 tie above Green 4. What rerolls, at what cost, and who bosses if both 5s reroll to 3? What if all largest tied dice belong to one player, or only smaller dice tie?
asked_facts_reviewed: Immediately reroll only tied largest dice at no cost.
If both become 3, Green unchanged 4 is boss; do not keep rerolling smaller 3s.
Same-player highest tie requires no reroll; ties below highest require none.
If different players remain tied for current highest, repeat with current highest until one player controls highest.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Current-highest cross-player dice only, free and immediate; Green4 wins when both5s become3; same-owner and subhighest ties exempt; repeat as needed.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p4 After Each Action Reroll if Tied and diagram

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: You have $18 and gamble at an opponent’s four-tile casino whose boss has $15. What is the maximum bet, who gets the House card, and how many times may you gamble this turn?
asked_facts_reviewed: Maximum $15: minimum of $20 tile cap, own $18 and boss $15.
Gamble once during own turn.
Give the casino boss the House card.
contextual_background_reviewed: Casino must be bossed by another player.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Maximum min($20,$18,$15)=$15; opposing boss gets House card; once on own turn. Given opposing eligibility stays contextual.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p4 Gamble

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: For a legal $4 bet against a boss who has $7, resolve every possible two-dice sum group, including the limited doubled payout. Is a winning bettor also losing their stake?
asked_facts_reviewed: 3/4/9/10/11: win $4 from boss and retain/get stake back.
2/12: nominal win $8 but receive only boss’s available $7 and retain/get stake back.
5/6/7/8: lose/pay $4 to boss.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Every2d6 sum correctly resolved: normal win4, doubled nominal8 limited to7, lose4; winning stake retained.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p4 Gamble; unified p13

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: What may be traded, when may trading occur, how are traded lots and dice transferred, and what cannot be promised or traded?
asked_facts_reviewed: Trade money, lots, casino dice and actions on the active player’s current turn. Trading may occur even off-turn, except no initiated trades during unresolved boss ties or after End of Game is drawn.
Replace lot marker with recipient marker; replace die with recipient die at same current pip value, not board value.
No points or casino tiles; no promises of future-turn actions/exchanges/transfers.
No actions on another player’s turn.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Base traded assets/current-turn actions, off-turn trades, marker/die transfer at current values, forbidden points/tiles/future promises/off-turn actions all correct. Broad timing now explicitly includes both unresolved-boss-tie and End-card prohibitions.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p4 Trading

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: Starting at score 8, where do single casino awards of 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 points leave you? Can two separate one-tile casinos combine their awards, and in what order are different casinos scored?
asked_facts_reviewed: 1 leaves 8; 2 or 3 reaches 10; 4 or 5 reaches 12.
Insufficient excess at a break is lost; cannot pool separate casino awards.
Score each casino independently smallest to largest, player chooses equal-size order; two single-tile awards leave 8.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: From8:1 stays8,2/3 reaches10,4/5 reaches12; excess loss, separate awards, ascending order and choice on equal sizes correct.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p2 Scoring; p3 scoring example and multiple casinos

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: What happens when the End of Game card is drawn, including remaining actions, final payouts, winner and tied score? Is there an immediate alternative win condition?
asked_facts_reviewed: Game ends immediately; no subsequent Play actions.
Final payout all owned lots and casinos touching Strip, with ordinary money and scoring rules.
Most points wins; tied most points breaks by most money.
90+ points wins immediately in base game.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Immediate end/no Play, final all marked lots and Strip casino money/points, score then money tie, base90+ instant win; no expansion end points.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p4 Winning; unified p16

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: In two-player play, what happens to F cards drawn during setup and during a turn? May anyone build on F, and can a turn pay more than once before actions?
asked_facts_reviewed: No building on F block.
Setup F card is discarded and replaced; valid two cards determine initial properties/money.
During turn do not mark F; pay owned lots and indicated casinos/points, discard then repeat Draw until A–E card resolved.
Each such draw pays, so multiple payouts occur in one turn before Play.
contextual_background_reviewed: An End of Game draw interrupts immediately; Q19 and Q32 test end priority.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: NoF building; setup discard/replaceF; turnF no marker but all instructed pay/score, discard and redraw untilA-E. Multiple payouts before Play correct.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p4 2-Player Rules/Winning; unified p16 2-Player Rules

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: All nine gold tiles are on the board. Can you build another gold tile using the spare tenth tile, sprawl a gold casino, or remodel a three-tile casino to gold? May you build a different available color?
asked_facts_reviewed: The tenth is a replacement, not a tenth usable tile.
Cannot build gold, sprawl gold or remodel to gold without sufficient available tiles.
Yes, a different available color may be built on an owned lot.
contextual_background_reviewed: Normal build cost applies; this question does not give a price or ask a monetary calculation.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Nine usable tiles, replacement tenth not extra; unavailable gold cannot build/sprawl/remodel; available other color legal. Unasked normal-price detail correctly contextual.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p1 Casino Tiles; p3 Available Tiles/Build/Sprawl/Remodel

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: All twelve of your dice are on the board when you build, sprawl or inherit a sprawled tile. How do you place the required die, what happens to the vacated tile and its scoring, and what if it was the casino’s only die?
asked_facts_reviewed: Remove one of your existing ownership dice and place it on the new tile at the value required by the placement.
Vacated tile remains ownerless but counts for casino points.
If no dice remain in a casino it has no owner/boss.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Relocate existing own die at placement-required value; vacated tile remains ownerless/scoring; no remaining die means no owner/boss. Optional trade route contextual.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p3 Available Dice; unified p6 Available Dice

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: A property draw claims a sprawled casino tile with no die; the board prints 2, while the die removed from it used to be 5. What die do you place, does the tile change, and when does its matching casino pay?
asked_facts_reviewed: Place own die at printed board value 2; former removed value 5 is not retained.
Casino tile remains; acquisition precedes matching casino payment.
contextual_background_reviewed: The new value2 die pays its owner $2 on that payout, but income amount is not asked here.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Own die uses board2, not former5; casino tile remains and acquisition precedes payment. Unasked $2 income calculation correctly contextual.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p2 Take Over Your Lot/Money Paid; unified p7

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: You draw the card for your own sprawled tile, whose die is now 6 although the board prints 2. Does ownership or value change, and what does that die earn if its casino pays?
asked_facts_reviewed: Leave your existing die unchanged at 6.
Matching payout pays you $6 for that die.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Own existing6 unchanged; $6 income when casino pays.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Unified p7 Step 2; original p2 Money Paid

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: All ten of your markers are on lots and you acquire another empty lot. How is ownership marked, what happens to the vacated lot, and which of the two lots receives the coming owned-lot payout?
asked_facts_reviewed: Move one existing marker to newly gained lot.
You no longer own vacated lot; it does not pay you lot income.
New marked lot pays you $1 in upcoming payout.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Relocate marker, lose old lot and its income, new marked lot pays $1; no invented marker supply.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Unified p6 Available Player Markers; original p2 Draw/Owned Lots Pay

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: May a player conceal money or piece counts, forbid inspection of a discard pile, or deny a bank payout because the physical bank is empty?
asked_facts_reviewed: Money, piece counts and discarded cards are public; anyone may inspect discards.
Bank money unlimited; physical bank exhaustion does not cancel a payout.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Public money/piece counts/discards and inspectable discard piles; unlimited bank. No disclosure of undrawn property-deck order implied.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p1 Money; unified p6 Your Resources/Available Money

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: A casino has two Red 6s and a Blue 3. During a trade one Red 6 is replaced by Green’s die. What value does Green’s die have, must anything reroll before further trades or actions, and who rolls?
asked_facts_reviewed: Green replacement remains 6.
Different players now tie for highest: immediately reroll both highest 6s (remaining Red and new Green), not Blue3.
Each owner rolls own tied dice; finish resolving current-highest cross-player ties before actions or initiating trades.
contextual_background_reviewed: Boss-tie rerolls are free; Q14 explicitly asks cost, Q27 does not.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Transferred die stays6; remainingRed6/newGreen6 roll, notBlue3; owners roll and finish before further actions/trades. Unasked free cost correctly contextual.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p4 Trading/Reroll if Tied; unified p9 Settling Who’s the Boss

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: You draw a card and replace one of Red’s tied highest 5s in a casino with your own 5; another Red 5 remains. Is the boss tie postponed until after payment or Play, and does this reroll count as a paid reorganization?
asked_facts_reviewed: Resolve cross-player highest tie immediately on takeover before casino payouts, not postponed to Play.
Reroll only current highest dice free; this is not paid reorganization and does not use its limit.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Takeover tie resolves before payout; current highest rolls free, separate from paid reorganization/limit.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Unified p7 Step 2/p9 Settling Who’s the Boss; p11 Reorganize

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: May you reorganize a casino where you alone own all dice, or one where you own none? Does reorganizing only one of your dice avoid paying for the opponents’ pips?
asked_facts_reviewed: Sole owner may reorganize; no-own-die casino may not.
Reorganization always rerolls every die and costs all pips, including opponents, not just selected own dice.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Sole ownership permits reorganization, zero own dice does not; no selective dice/pip payment.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p3 Reorganize; unified p11

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: All twelve of your ownership dice are on casino tiles. Must you remove a tile’s die just to gamble, and may you gamble at your own casino if no opponent bosses any casino?
asked_facts_reviewed: Any dice may be used to gamble; no ownership placement or removal required for the gambling roll.
Cannot gamble at own casino; if no opponent bosses a casino there is no legal gambling action.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Any dice may gamble without displacing ownership dice; cannot gamble at own casino or without opponent-bossed host.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Unified p6 Available Dice; p13 Gamble

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: On your turn you trade for an opponent’s die so that you can reorganize their casino, then promise to pay them for a sprawl only if the reorganization gives you control. If the reroll does not make you boss so the agreed sprawl cannot happen, do the subsequent steps of the trade proceed? Could the opponent instead perform the sprawl on your turn?
asked_facts_reviewed: When an element of trade is prevented, subsequent steps do not occur.
Cannot sprawl without boss control.
Opponent cannot take action on your turn.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Failed same-turn conditional step halts subsequent trade steps; active player needs boss control to sprawl; opponent cannot act off-turn. Scope note preserves intended actor/turn.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Unified p15 Trading; original p3 Sprawl/p4 Trading

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: The End of Game card has just been drawn. Before the final payout, may players initiate a last-minute trade of money or a casino die, perhaps to change who wins a tied score?
asked_facts_reviewed: No: End of Game draw immediately ends play, so players cannot initiate a money/die trade before final payouts.
contextual_background_reviewed: Final lots and Strip payouts, score/money win comparison are already asked by Q19; they are not additional requirements for this trade-priority question.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: No initiated money/die trade once End card drawn, even before final payout. Unasked payout/winner recap correctly contextual.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p4 Winning; unified physical p16 Winning, first paragraph (no actions or initiated trades on End of Game draw).

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: During setup, which pieces does each player take, and where is each player’s scoring chip placed before the first turn?
asked_facts_reviewed: Each player takes an action card and the scoring chip, markers and dice of one player color. Place every player’s scoring chip on 0 on the scoring track.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Each takes matching-color action card/chip/markers/dice and puts score chip at0.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p2 Setting Up, first and third paragraphs; unified physical p5 Setting Up.

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: Must a trade be between exactly two players, or may three players participate in one agreed trade of their money, lots and casino dice?
asked_facts_reviewed: Any number of players may be involved in a trade, so a three-player trade is permitted, subject to the ordinary restrictions on traded assets and timing.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Any number of participants permits three-player base-asset trade. Explicit scope note prevents ordinary-restriction recap becoming extra requirements.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Unified physical p15 At Any Time: Trading, first paragraph: any number of players may be involved. Original p4 Trading supplies base assets and restrictions.

per_question_scope_key_findings.question: Besides taking their own components, what banking role must the group assign during setup?
asked_facts_reviewed: Choose a player to be the Banker.
per_question_scope_key_findings.analysis: Choose a player as Banker: directly asked and expressly supported by originalp2/unifiedp5. No invented selection priority or extra Banker duties.
per_question_scope_key_findings.source_references: Original p2 Setting Up, second paragraph; unified physical p5 Setting Up.
